title: Routing declaration cookbook and rollout matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on cookbook for declaring routing rules, validating them (CI + runtime), and a practical rollout matrix tailored to multi-region, multi-model inference pipelines. Aim: reduce friction for engineers writing rules while codifying safe gating patterns for production change windows.

Audience:
- Platform engineers authoring control-plane configs
- Oncall/SREs who review rollouts
- Solutions engineers defining customer-specific fallbacks

Overview / goals:
- Provide a minimal canonical structure for route declarations (examples in YAML + JSON).
- Surface common edge cases and how to test them locally.
- Offer a rollout matrix mapping risk level -> required gates (lint, unit tests, staging canary, telemetry checks).
- Describe automated validation steps (pre-commit, CI, and runtime guards).

Quick reference: canonical fields (flat list)
- id: stable-uuid-or-slug (immutable once live)
- name: human-friendly
- priority: integer (higher wins; default 0)
- match: type + pattern (path | header | region | model_capability)
- route_to: model_id or pool_id or fallback_chain[]
- sticky_kv: optional key to maintain session affinity
- region_affinity: list of region codes / null for global
- experiments: optional map of variant percentages
- rollout_policy: {type: immediate|canary|staged} (declared, enforced by control plane)
- created_by, created_at, description, tags

Example: simple YAML declaration (good for quick authoring)
---
- id: route-search-long-context-v3
  name: "search-long-context-v3 - primary path for long-cntx"
  priority: 50
  match:
    type: path_prefix
    pattern: "/api/generate/search"
  route_to:
    - model_id: rdx-mpt-30b-q8
      percent: 100
  region_affinity: ["us-west1", "us-east1"]
  rollout_policy:
    type: canary
    canary_steps:
      - duration_minutes: 30
        percent: 5
      - duration_minutes: 60
        percent: 25
      - duration_minutes: 120
        percent: 100
  description: "Handles search generation calls where long context is expected"
---

JSON Schema snippet (authoring-time validator)
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "match", "route_to"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9-._]{3,64}$"},
    "priority": {"type": "integer"},
    "match": {"type": "object"},
    "route_to": {"type": "array"}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

(We enforce this schema in the authoring linter; expand before shipping if new fields are introduced.)

Validation checks (CI + preflight)
- Lint (json-schema): required fields exist, id pattern, no unknown properties.
- No duplicate ids in same namespace.
- Priority collisions: warn if two rules with identical match scope have same priority.
- Region coverage analysis: ensure every rule with region_affinity has fallback to a global route or another region.
- Model compatibility check: the declared model_id must exist in catalog and support the requested capabilities (embedding vs generation).
- Immutable-field check: changes to id or created_by are rejected; changes to priority flagged for review.
- Canary sanity: canary percent steps must be strictly increasing and final step must be 100%.

Edge cases and how to test them
1) Overlapping path prefixes
   - Problem: "/api/generate" vs "/api/generate/search".
   - Test: unit test matcher resolution order; expect longer, more specific prefix to win when priority equal.
   - Lint rule: warn on overlapping prefixes with similar priority; suggest explicit priority.

2) Circular fallback chains
   - Problem: rule A falls back to B, B falls back to A.
   - Test: graph cycle detection in CI; reject cycles.

3) Regional leftover with no fallback
   - Problem: rule bound to eu-west1 but no fallback and no dedicated capacity -> errors during capacity scheduling.
   - Test: capacity placement simulation in staging.

4) Model pinning vs autoswap
   - Problem: customer pins model to rdx-mpt-30b-v1 but autoswap policy might swap to quantized rdx-mpt-30b-q4.
   - Authoring guidance: use route_to entries with explicit compatibility tags and an "upgrade_allowed: boolean" flag.

Rollout matrix (risk -> gates)
- Low (documentation/alpha-only routes): Lint + unit tests -> merge.
- Medium (non-customer-facing defaults): Lint + unit tests + staging canary 1% for 1h + telemetry smoke tests (latency, error rate) -> merge after pass.
- High (customer SLA-affecting, region change, model replacement): Lint + unit tests + full canary per region with progressive ramp (5 -> 25 -> 100) + 24h metrics observation + SRE signoff via PR comment.
- Emergency change (hotfix): Control-plane allows immediate apply but requires post-mortem and a revert schedule within 2 hours.

Automated gating pipeline (recommended)
1) pre-commit: json-schema lint + id uniqueness check (local cache).
2) CI PR: run full authoring lints, run matcher unit tests, region placement simulation, model-compat check.
3) staging pipeline: apply to staging control plane with synthetic traffic per rule; collect: p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokens/sec, queue depth.
4) canary automation: uses rollout_policy canary_steps to increment percentages; monitors defined telemetry queries; auto-rolls-back on triggers.

Sample telemetry queries (PromQL-like syntax)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route_id=~"%s"}[5m])) by (le))
- error rate: sum(rate(requests_total{route_id="%s",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{route_id="%s"}[5m]))
- token cost delta: increase(token_cost_total{route_id="%s"}[15m])

Canary failure triggers (examples)
- p95 latency increases > 2x baseline for 10 min
- error rate > 0.5% absolute increase AND > 25% relative increase
- token cost increase > 30% without quality improvement flag

Runtime guards (control-plane enforcement)
- Reject apply if cycle detected in fallback graph.
- Enforce immutable fields.
- If route_to references model not in catalog, treat as "pending" and block activation.
- If canary_policy present, control-plane will only accept the declaration and schedule canary; manual patch bypasses allowed only by SRE.

Local tooling hacks (dev experience)
- rdxctl validate path/to/routing.yaml  # runs schema + quick graph checks
- rdxctl simulate path/to/routing.yaml --region us-west1 --qps 50 # returns placement + estimated latency impact
- rdxctl diff --live route-id # diff against live control-plane rule

Testing checklist before merge
- [ ] json-schema lint pass
- [ ] no id duplicate in repo
- [ ] priority sanity check run
- [ ] model compatibility check passed
- [ ] region fallback verified
- [ ] unit tests for matcher resolution included

Open questions / TODOs
- Define a machine-readable "capability" map from model artifacts -> supported match types (e.g., function-calling, streaming, structured-output). (Related: PLAT-3010)
- Decide default behavior for overlapping matches when priorities are equal (we currently prefer specificity but it must be explicit).
- Add a formal cost-estimate field on route objects to let Optimize make proactive recommendations.

Appendix: authoritative examples and negative tests
1) Negative: canary steps not increasing -> rejected.
2) Negative: route id with uppercase -> rejected by id pattern.
3) Negative: circular fallback -> rejected.
4) Positive: layered fallback: primary -> regional replica -> global fallback (each has capacity tag)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic with concrete examples to reduce back-and-forth. If you add fields, update the JSON Schema and the rdxctl validators.
- Prefer small, iterative rollouts; prefer many small routes over one mega-rule with many branches.

Scribes: Maya Chen (author), Lucas Patel (validation harness), Aisha Gomez (telemetry queries)
